title: Mansfield District Council Sustainability Appraisal / Environmental Outcomes Report of the Local Plan
description:
Nottinghamshire County Council (the Council) is seeking tenders, on behalf of Mansfield District Council (MDC),

MDC is commencing the next Mansfield District Local Plan review as required by statutory legislation. In order to provide a suitable basis for progressing the plan, the District Council is seeking tender quotations from suitably qualified and experienced consultants to undertake a Sustainability Appraisal (SA) incorporating Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) / Environmental Outcomes Report (EOR). The SA / EOR is required by legislation, the National Planning Policy Framework and Planning Practice Guidance and to meet the legal tests of Local Plan Examination. These requirements ensure the Local Plan is a sustainable plan.

MDC is located in the north western part of the County of Nottinghamshire. It covers an area of some 30 square miles (77 Square kilometres). Mansfield is the main town within the district, but other settlements include: Mansfield Woodhouse, Forest Town, Market Warsop and the surrounding Warsop Parish villages and parts of Pleasley, Clipston and Rainworth. Mansfield District has an estimated population of 108,576. This represents 13.28% of the Nottinghamshire County population of 817, 841.

title: MANSFIELD DISTRICT COUNCIL SMART PARKING
description:
Nottinghamshire County Council (the Council) is seeking tenders, on behalf of Mansfield District Council (MDC),

As a part of its Town Investment Plan, Mansfield District Council (MDC) is investing in several projects to improve Mansfield Town Centre and Mansfield District as a place to live, work and visit. A key objective is to increase foot fall and dwell time in the town centre to improve its economic prosperity. One key project within the portfolio is the upgrading of the existing car parks in the town, towards a modern Smart Parking infrastructure. The vision is to provide Smart Parking infrastructure that is easy to use, is inclusive and uses modern technology. It will be easier and more efficient for MDC to manage. It will be a key tool in increasing use of the town centre for work, shopping, leisure and tourism.
Ideally MDC wants to include 13 car parks (2 multi-storey and 11 surface) in the scope of the smart parking project. There is a limited capital budget for this project, if the budget does not cover the installation of the Smart Parking infrastructure in all 13 car parks, the priority is for the two multi-storey car parks to be completed initially. The order of priority after the 2 multi-storey carparks will be based on the capacity of the car parks from high to low. Table 3.1 in this document shows the capacity of all car parks that fall within this project.
MDC intends to appoint a turnkey supplier that can design and install all elements of the required solution, and as many of the desired elements detailed later in this document.
It is assumed that the project will take less than 8 months from contract commencement date.
It is assumed that suppliers tendering for the project will have relevant experience. Suppliers should highlight relevant association and professional memberships such as British Parking Association.

Bassetlaw District Council is the northernmost of Nottinghamshire's Councils and is home to over 118,000 people. The purpose of the DWDC will be to establish a locally distinctive framework that identifies locally important design principles for the district, with a focus upon appropriate requirements and guidance to facilitate the delivery of development as identified by the Local Plan spatial strategy including Local Plan allocations. The Coal Authority (Client) was established by Parliament to undertake specific statutory duties, set out in the Coal Industry Act 1994, associated with licensing coal mining operations; managing property and the historic legacy arising from the ownership of the coal reserves and underground workings; settling subsidence damage claims not falling on coal mine operators and providing access to coal mining information.

The Coal Authority has a legal duty under the Coal Mining Subsidence Act 1991, to repair properties damaged by coal mining subsidence in the five coalfield regions. The works are funded by grant in aid from central government, in order that the Coal Authority can discharge its statutory duty.

The Coal Authority employs over 300 people, based mainly at the head office in Mansfield with some field staff remotely based in order to enable a fast response to incidents in the coal mining areas.

The Coal Authority is funded by grant in aid from the Department of Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ)

We are publishing this Framework opportunity to retender our Ground Investigation Framework, 

The Coal Authority requires the provision of Ground investigation services which includes general items, boreholes, rotary drilling, pits and trenches, sampling, in-situ testing, geophysical testing, instrumentation and monitoring, laboratory testing, chemical testing for contaminated ground and attendance at framework meetings with the Client.

The works required under this framework will be located throughout the British coalfield areas which are split across the following five regions.

• Region 1 - Scotland East and West

• Region 2 - Cumbria / Northumberland / Co.Durham / Durham / Sunderland / Newcastle

• Region 3 - North Wales / Cheshire / Lancashire / Merseyside / North Yorkshire / West Yorkshire

• Region 4 - South Yorkshire / Nottinghamshire / Derbyshire / Leicestershire / Staffordshire / Shropshire / West Midlands / Warwickshire / Herefordshire / Worcestershire

• Region 5 - Somerset / South Gloucestershire / Bristol / South Wales / Pembrokeshire / North Gloucestershire (Forest of Dean)

These regions correspond with the UK Coal Fields. There may also be requirement for Ground Investigation within Mid Wales for examination of Metal mining fields.

The framework scope is the provision of ground investigation works and includes general items, boreholes, rotary drilling, pits and trenches, sampling, in-situ testing, geophysical testing, instrumentation and monitoring, laboratory testing, chemical testing for contaminated ground and attendance at framework meetings with the Client.

Interested parties can register for free ahead via the Coal Authority's Tender Portal Inbye at the following address:

https://inbye.coal.gov.uk/s2c/

Use of the system is Free of Charge but will require some company information and agreement to terms and conditions to access the system.

description:
This project was a further competition procedure under the dynamic purchasing system Domestic Abuse Safe Accommodation Support Services Dynamic Provider List, project reference DN571003. It was run in accordance with the Public Contract Regulations 2015 and was a Light Touch Procurement for social and other specific services.
To ensure the appropriate types and coverage of refuge provision across the County bids were sought for three Lots.
LOT 1, South Nottinghamshire, covers Ashfield district and Broxtowe, Gedling and Rushcliffe boroughs.  The requirement was for communal accommodation, with or without additional dispersed accommodation.
LOT 2, Countywide required dispersed accommodation across the County of Nottinghamshire.
LOT 3, North Nottinghamshire, covers Mansfield, Newark and Sherwood and Bassetlaw districts.  The requirement was for communal accommodation, with or without additional dispersed accommodation.
The aim of the services is to provide comprehensive specialist support services for female survivors of domestic abuse and their children residing in domestic abuse safe accommodation.  This will include ensuring the highest degree of safety and security for survivors residing in the accommodation, offering individual support to meet the assessed needs of Survivors and aid their recovery, supporting Survivors to access other services to meet their physical and mental health needs, supporting Survivors and encouraging them to make independent decisions about their lives and being responsive to the needs of children and young people, ensuring they receive the right support to deal with the trauma they have endured.
Services will be delivered within safe accommodation, refuges, which may be individual units, dispersed housing or communal refuges.

description:
The NTU Institute of Health and Allied Professions department is seeking to appoint a Supplier to provide a service to design and deliver all Moving and Handling training requirements for students undertaking pre-registration/undergraduate health professional courses at the institute. 

Due to the practice placement requirements within these programmes we need to ensure that students are fully trained for safe Moving and Handling of patients within the health and social care services where they are based. The training fulfils mandatory requirements for the University and organisations where the students will undertake placement. The successful supplier needs to be able to supply a full on-campus service to comprehensively cover the theoretical, legislative knowledge and practical skills students require to safely undertake Moving and Handling activities in a range of healthcare environments.   

We are appointing a supplier external to the institute to offer specialist skills and experience in the field of Moving and Handling. The institute is a newly formed department within NTU where we have introduced new programmes for students wishing to develop careers in health, including education in the field of Nursing Associates, Ambulance Technicians, Paramedics, Adult, Mental Health and Learning Disabilities Nursing. Our education programmes are delivered across multiple sites and the supplier will undertake delivery at NTU Clifton Campus and NTU Hub at Mansfield (Vision West Nottinghamshire College Campus).

We are continuing to validate and develop new programmes and are seeking a supplier to offer quality provision of Moving and Handling training to these students.

description:

The Provider is required to arrange for a qualified and accredited pharmacist to consult with clients attending for EHC. If deemed to be clinically appropriate, the pharmacist can supply either the hormonal post coital contraception Levonorgestrel 1.5mg or Ulipristal acetate 30mg to individuals requesting the EHC and who are clinically eligible and give consent. \r
\r
Providers of the service must be registered with the General Pharmaceutical Council (GPhC) and completed training to provide this service.  \r

title: Vehicle Recovery Services
description:
Greater Manchester Police have an obligation to ensure the free passageway of the highways and the physical removal of those vehicles where there is a likelihood of danger or obstruction to other road users.

Legislation empowers the Police to remove or arrange for the removal of vehicles which are abandoned, damaged, causing obstruction or danger as well as those that are suspected stolen.  Invariably, Recovery Operators are called upon to assist the Police in the recovery, storage and final disposal of these vehicles.

Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) is tendering to appoint operators to deliver light and heavy vehicle recovery services within the Greater Manchester area. The contract period will be 2 years with an option to extend for a further 3 years on a 1 + 1 + 1 option. 

To be considered for award of a contract Recovery Operators must have in place the relevant operator licences, accreditations and Health and Safety policies. The contract will also be broken down into various Lots to cover a variety of geographical areas in Greater Manchester. Where there are multiple operators awarded to any of the lots, jobs will be allocated evenly on a pro-rota basis starting with the highest scoring bidders.
